parent_v14.key_result: exact outcome-adaptive REL/FP/KO trees weakly dominated the best fixed equal-cost panels, with strict worst-case savings in 262 row-target combinations and widespread branch-specific replanning

scientific_question: Does target-aware adaptive relational evidence remain advantageous when relational measurement families have different predeclared costs, and do analyst choices about evidence cost change which measurement should be taken first?

analysis_base.worlds: exact frozen v12 random static-equivalent topology worlds
analysis_base.atomic_measurements: exact unchanged v13/v14 REL, FP and KO measurements

cost_semantics.family_from_action_id: REL:* -> REL, FP:* -> FP, KO:* -> KO
cost_semantics.additivity: total path cost is the sum of action-family costs along that branch

fixed_reference.definition: minimum total cost of one nonadaptive set of measurements sufficient to identify the target for every world in the row
fixed_reference.tie_rule: minimum total cost, then fewer measurements, then lexicographically smallest sorted action tuple

adaptive_planner.target_stop_rule: stop when all surviving worlds share the declared target value
adaptive_planner.objective: minimize worst-case remaining total cost under the current cost world
adaptive_planner.transition: after an action outcome, retain worlds with that exact deterministic measurement value
adaptive_planner.tie_rule: minimum worst-case cost, then lexicographically smallest action ID
adaptive_planner.repeated_action_rule: an already observed deterministic action cannot split its child state again

secondary_realized_summary.definition: mean realized total cost of the canonical worst-case-cost-optimal adaptive policy when each of the 12 declared worlds is counted once
secondary_realized_summary.claim_boundary: descriptive finite-panel average, not an ecological prior

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every row, target and cost world, exact adaptive worst-case total cost is <= the exact minimum fixed-panel total cost.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Each of the four cost worlds has at least one row-target combination with adaptive worst-case cost strictly below the best fixed-panel cost.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED separately for any cost world without a strict saving.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target combination has a different canonical first action under two predeclared cost worlds.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if canonical first action is invariant to all cost worlds everywhere.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For each family X in {REL,FP,KO}, making X expensive strictly reduces the pooled frequency with which an X action is canonical first relative to the equal-cost world.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED separately for any family without a strict decrease.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every row and cost world, adaptive worst-case cost for pairwise_relation, first_passage, intervention and critical_node_count is <= full_topology_identity cost.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every cost world, at least one row has intervention or critical_node_count adaptive worst-case cost strictly below full_topology_identity cost.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED separately for a cost world without such a row.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Every cost world has at least one row-target policy choosing different second actions after different first-action outcomes.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED separately if a cost world reduces every optimal policy to one fixed order.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Every row-target-cost-world combination remains exactly resolvable using only the unchanged REL/FP/KO library.

secondary_outputs: fixed and adaptive total-cost distributions by target and cost world
first-action and first-family frequencies by cost world
rows where the cheapest policy uses more measurements than the equal-cost minimum
claim_boundary: Cost worlds are analyst sensitivity scenarios, not calibrated field budgets.
A cost-optimal synthetic policy is not automatically a practical sampling protocol.
Generic cost-sensitive decision trees are not claimed as new; the ecological question is whether EOG relational evidence recommendations are robust to plausible cost ordering.
No post-score cost tuning is allowed.
stop_rules: Do not change 1-versus-3 family costs after scoring.
Do not add a fifth cost world after scoring.
Do not make costs target-specific after scoring.
Do not replace worst-case cost with expected cost after scoring.
